title: Who Set the Speed Limit
summary: SAID: Secretary of State Marco Rubio at Joint Base Andrews Sat Oct 17: nobody in the US ordered Starlink speeds slowed in Ukraine, 'it sort of happened'. Rubio in Mumbai Wed Oct 21: 'this decision' is governed by a private commercial contract, what speeds they allow; 'we cannot direct a private company'; Starshield is sold and operated through the Department of War. Musk Oct 14: Starshield is owned and controlled by the US government, limits by the military and ultimately POTUS. Hegseth Oct 20: that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions. Trump Oct 16: 'I don't know if it was anybody' (full cut). DONE: Ukraine's defense ministry (interested party): military Starshield terminals cut out above about 161 km/h since Oct 14; CBS Oct 20-21: Zelensky's office says still throttled. Contract text not published. Receipts: 2022 SpaceX letter asking the Pentagon to fund Ukraine terminals (CNN), Musk 'the hell with it... free', Pentagon confirms contracting June 1 2023 (Defense News); Musk Sep 7 2023 on refusing an emergency request to activate Starlink to Sevastopol. Full cut adds what changed since Tuesday (UKMTO 179/180-26, SPR 282.7M bbl, OFAC GL 131K moving the Lukoil deadline to Nov 21, Nebraska fuel EO, Witkoff).

title: Ninety-Five Percent of What
summary: SAID: CENTCOM spokesman Tim Hawkins told Al Jazeera Tue Oct 20 (9:33 AM ET) the Strait of Hormuz is "open and secure" and 95% of ships cross safely, with no denominator or start date. The IRGC said its mines set two tankers ablaze, and IRNA later claimed a third (a VLCC); none named a hull or time. CENTCOM called the mine claims false and said lanes were cleared. DONE: CENTCOM's own Sat Oct 17 count is 138 ships redirected; Kpler counts at least 18 vessels under fire in two weeks; UKMTO says most attacked vessels go unreported, so every official count is a floor; UKMTO advisory 178-26 logged a military interaction with a tanker off Duqm; the SPR is at 282.7M bbl, the lowest since 1982. Receipts: the 1988 Navy formal investigation of USS Vincennes / Iran Air 655 (290 dead) found the Aegis system's performance "excellent - it functioned as designed" and said Iran must share responsibility; Capt. Rogers later got the Legion of Merit with a citation that omits the airliner; the NSA historian (Hanyok, declassified 2005) found no attack on Aug 4 1964 in the Gulf of Tonkin. Full cut adds markets, Wright/Bessent, and what changed since Oct 19 (Munir in Tehran, Netanyahu's "job to finish", two Riyadh intercepts + UK Typhoons, State of Israel ad time in Des Moines via Parscale's foreign-agent filing, set to air Saturday).
